title: Avantara Saint Cloud ranks 3rd in Pennington County nursing home size for Q1 2026
text:
Avantara Saint Cloud ranked as the third largest nursing facility in Pennington County for the first quarter of 2026, according to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) .
The facility had a total bed count of 78, which is 11 more than Pennington County’s average for the same period. They provided care to an average of 70.2 residents during that time.
The CMS gave Avantara Saint Cloud an overall rating of 1 out of 5, which falls below the South Dakota nursing home average of 2.8.
For the quarter, Avantara Mountain View was the largest nursing home in Pennington County with 101 beds, while Fountain Springs Healthcare ranked second, offering 90 beds.
As of the end of the first quarter of 2026, Avantara Saint Cloud recorded a total of $11,408 in one fine and incurred one penalty.
There were five for-profit nursing homes operating in Pennington County, South Dakota in total.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the nation’s older adult population continues to rise while the size of younger age groups shrinks. From 2020 through 2024, Americans age 65 and older grew by 13%, while those under 18 dropped by 1.7%. The population of Americans 65 and older has expanded significantly in the last century, from 4.9 million in 1920 to over 61 million by 2024.
Research from 2021 forecasts that nearly half of the nation’s adults 65 or older, about 28 million people, are likely to require long-term services and supports, with more than one-third anticipated to eventually need care in a nursing home.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
